title: Estimation of the radiant performance of flame-retardant fabrics considering thermal degradation effect
journal: Journal of Engineered Fibers and Fabrics 14
treatment_method: Commercial inherently flame-resistant fabric, used in its virgin state and conditioned according to GB/T 6529-2008. No added flame-retardant finish or durability washing is reported.
LOI_specimen_preparation: Virgin fabric specimens 120 × 60 mm, marked 50 mm from the ignition side; conditioned according to GB/T 6529-2008. Each LOI test repeated five times and mean reported.
TG_locator: Original Table 2, Thermal degradation performance value of TG and DTG: Tmax, R500, R700 and R800. The table explicitly defines Tmax as the temperature at maximum thermal degradation rate.
LOI_locator: Original Table 3, Test results of flame resistance performance: PSA 29.4%, Nomex IIIA 28.5%. Experimental LOI paragraph reports five repeated tests and mean values.
conditions_locator: Original Experimental section: Fabric materials, Thermal analysis tests and Flame-retardant tests; Table 1 fabric construction. Dry N2 at 25 mL/min, 10 K/min, 20-800 °C.
pairing_evidence: The Experimental section defines the same two virgin fabric specimens used in TG and LOI. Tables 2 and 3 repeat the identical PSA and Nomex IIIA labels. Convective pre-exposure and charred fabrics are subsequently introduced for thermal protective and optical tests, and no charred-state LOI or TG pair is proposed.
source_location: Complete original publisher HTML: Experimental sections and Tables 1-3; Table 2 also indexed in original PDF p 5. Tables 4 onward concern separate convective/radiant exposure tests. No PDF document hash or pixel access claim.
limitations: Two virgin fabric states. Warp and weft columns in Table 3 concern vertical burning properties; each fabric has one measured LOI, not separate directional states. LOI is the mean of five tests without a reported SD. General fabric conditioning cites GB/T 6529-2008; the later 24 h, 20 ± 2 °C and 65 ± 5% RH conditioning statement is within the thermal-protection method and is not silently assigned to TG or LOI. Nomex secondary degradation is described only as 560-570 °C and is not converted to a numerical peak. Charred and thermally exposed fabrics lack separate matching LOI/TG evidence and are held. TPP and radiant-test mass loss are excluded from TGA. No graph estimation or MCC substitution.
source_material_form_TGA_raw: TG and DTG curves of virgin PSA and Nomex IIIA fabrics in dry nitrogen.
source_numeric_evidence_description: Original publisher Table 2 defines Tmax as the temperature of maximum thermal degradation rate and gives carbon residue percentages at 500, 700 and 800 °C. Table 3 gives directly measured mean LOI.
source_title: Estimation of the radiant performance of flame-retardant fabrics considering thermal degradation effect
